# SK1012 — Use a switch expression for a returning equality chain

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A chain of constant equality tests returning values of the same type can use a switch expression.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 8.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Switch expressions express a value selected from alternatives. This rule preserves evaluation count by requiring one stable input, unique constant patterns, an explicit fallback, and identity-converted results of one type. It does not guess at numeric common-type inference, boxing, target typing or custom conversions.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
int M(int x) { if (x == 0) return 10; else if (x == 1) return 20; else return 30; }
```

Write:

```csharp
int M(int x) => x switch { 0 => 10, 1 => 20, _ => 30 };
```

## When it does not fire

Only if/else-if/else chains with at least two equality tests on one uncaptured, non-ref local/parameter are supported. Every body must contain only a value return. Integral, enum and string constant tests are supported; duplicate constants and exhaustive bool cases are excluded. Results must have identical actual and converted types across every branch. Comments, directives, custom equality, missing fallbacks, custom conversions, ref returns, caller-argument-expression capture and ambiguous pattern identifiers are excluded. Constant dependencies must be metadata constants or declared in this source file, including transitive initializers, so cached findings do not depend on another source file's body.
